Comfort, Encouragement, Direction, Peace. I’ve been with Dwell for several years now, and like many other apps, it has grown and offers new material every so often, while remaining rich and meaningful. What I like best: Dwell Daily, Anglican readings for Advent, Lent, and praying, Malcolm Guite’s readings, and reading through (or listening to) the Scriptures with options for translations or voices. In addition, they have readings for kids, which my grandson now enjoys. Dwell was introduced to me in 2020, I think, during a period of grief and trauma in my life, and it became a kind of lifeline for me and my husband. I have introduced strangers and friends to the app simply because I believe it is the best app out there for help in times of struggle and growing in God’s grace. Many thanks to John, who introduced me to the app, and the staff who contribute to Dwell Daily each morning. 
If you are looking for an app that provides truth, rich teachings, comfort and encouragement, look no further than the Dwell app. May it be a blessing to you as it has been to us.

Appreciate the Features, Concerned About the Content. I really appreciate the features of the Dwell app, especially the ability to make playlists, use CarPlay, and listen to Scripture throughout my day. These tools help me stay rooted in God's Word.

That said, I have some concerns about certain parts of the app. As a Bible-believing Christian, I want to stay away from practices that resemble New Age or mystical spirituality. Some of the content, like breath prayers and Lectio Divina, feels more emotional or contemplative than scriptural. I’ve noticed a few reflections that shift the focus away from God’s Word and instead direct people toward experiences or inner impressions.

I still use the app, but I intentionally avoid those sections. I would love to see a version of Dwell that focuses solely on Scripture readings, with no added prayer prompts or meditative practices. That kind of content would give users like me full confidence in what we’re hearing and sharing with others.

Thank you for creating a platform that makes listening to the Bible more accessible. I pray that the content continues to grow in a direction that keeps God's Word at the center.
